text:
carla: quick q — we're finalizing the embeddings contract for mixed batches. couple of specific things i want to lock down: 1) do we preserve empty-string items in the output ordering (i.e., return a vector for them), 2) per-item truncation vs reject whole batch when an item > max_tokens, and 3) can we add a non-breaking way to surface truncation warnings to clients?

mike: good call. current prod behavior (legacy) is to silently truncate items longer than limit and still return positions, so clients get same-length output. no explicit warnings. that's bitten some users though.

jess: @carla i'd vote we preserve ordering and return something for empty items — consistent positional mapping is important for downstream indexing. options: return a deterministic embedding for empty string, or a zero vector + metadata. zero vector can be confusing (is it real?).

sam: for truncation i prefer per-item truncation with a per-item warning array in the response. whole-batch reject is surprising in multi-tenant pipelines; better to be forgiving and surface metadata.

carla: agreed on preserving positions. for the warning surface i sketched a minimal design that should be backwards-compatible: add top-level optional `warnings` array of strings and a parallel `item_warnings` array aligned to inputs. existing clients that ignore unknown keys continue to work. example: ```json
{
  "data": [ {"embedding": [0.1, ...]}, {"embedding": [0.0,...]}, ... ],
  "item_warnings": [null, "truncated: token_count=1536 > 1024", null],
  "warnings": ["1 item truncated"]
}
```

mike: small nit — some SDKs parse `data` strictly. adding keys is ok, but we should also avoid changing vector shapes or ordering. confirm vector length never changes for the same model/version.

jess: +1. we must guarantee embedding dimensionality invariant per model version. any plan to return a sentinel vector (all zeros) for empty input? i worry about semantic collisions.

sam: proposal: deterministic embedding for empty string (compute with canonical empty input pipeline) and add `item_warnings` entry of "empty_input" for those. That way clients can detect and handle specially.

mike: sounds reasonable. infra note: we need integration tests for: empty item preserved, item_warnings alignment, per-item truncation, and warning population. i'll add tests in `embed_integration_test.py`.

carla: awesome. one more thing — batch splitting behavior when client sends > max_batch_items. do we split behind the scenes keeping order, or return 413/too_many_items?

jess: we currently auto-shard large batches (up to a limit) to avoid client-side splitting. but we should document exactly when we do it. policy: if total_items <= hard_limit (e.g., 10k) we split and preserve order; if > hard_limit return 413. phrase it as "server-side sharding up to X items, beyond that reject".

sam: implementation detail: ensure `item_warnings` is concatenated in same order after sharding — i.e., merge per-shard warnings into the final item_warnings array before returning. add tests for that.

carla: PR plan: i'll open a docs PR that describes `item_warnings` + `warnings` and the sharding policy. @mike can you add the server change for adding `item_warnings` and the truncation flag? @sam can you add tests and a quick SDK patch to surface `item_warnings` in Python SDK?

mike: yep. i'll prep a small compat shim so old clients don't explode if they pass strict JSON validators. will target `infra/main` branch.

sam: i'll pick up tests. tentative PRs: docs -> github.com/redwood/docs/pull/512, infra -> github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1423, sdk -> github.com/redwood/sdk-python/pull/211.

infra-bot: CI queued for github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1423 (embed tests).

jess: thanks all. one follow-up: add a simple example in docs for client-side handling: check `item_warnings[i] == "truncated"` and optionally re-chunk input. small snippet in docs helps.

carla: agreed. action items: docs PR with examples (carla), infra change adding item_warnings & deterministic empty embedding (mike), tests + SDK surface (sam). we'll sync in async — if any blocker ping here or DM. :thumbsup:
